summary: You take the required courses (DLCL 301 and 369, SLAVIC 300B, 230, 379 and 311) for a letter grade, and the 135 units count only graduate-level courses. The 14 Slavic seminars and three related-field courses are moved in by hand, and the proficiency test, qualifying exams and paper, related field exam, candidacy, oral exam, dissertation, language requirement and the expected B+ in each course are checked by hand.

program.why: Grading: "PhD students in the department must take required courses for a letter grade if available". The expected B+ is reviewed by the faculty ("The grade stands, and the student's academic performance is monitored"), not a floor on what counts.

totals.label: Courses below the graduate level
totals.why: "All courses counted toward the 135-unit requirement for the Ph.D. must be at the graduate level." Read as courses taken under a listing numbered below 200 that is not a graduate listing; the required SLAVIC 230 has no graduate listing but is numbered 230.

Qguue8Gq.why: "Unless they have taken such courses elsewhere, students must take the departmental course on medieval literature, 18th-century literature, and Old Church Slavonic." SLAVIC 379 and SLAVIC 230 are listed already; the departmental Old Church Slavonic course is SLAVIC 311 ("Introduction to Old Church Slavonic"). A course taken elsewhere is moved in. Grading: "PhD students in the department must take required courses for a letter grade if available".
